sections.h2: What should a seller know about Effingham County, Georgia?
sections.html:
Effingham County is a fast-growing part of the Savannah metropolitan area, with Springfield as the county seat and Rincon as the largest city. It was one of Georgia's original counties, created February 5, 1777, and Springfield was established in 1799 (Wikipedia). Guyton and Rincon are the other two cities, and Clyo, Egypt, Meldrim and Shawnee are unincorporated communities.

The Census Bureau counted 64,769 residents in 2020 and estimated 74,397 for July 2025, a gain of 14.8 percent over the 2020 base. Among the four Georgia counties in its latest QuickFacts comparison, Effingham has the highest median home value at $276,000 and the highest median household income at $88,438. About 78.4 percent of homes are owner-occupied, and the average commute runs 32.3 minutes.

For a seller, that growth means a deep pool of buyers who commute toward Savannah. It also means the county's tax bill has been a political topic, which is covered below.

sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Effingham County?
sections.html:
Two offices split the work: the Board of Tax Assessors sets values and the Tax Commissioner bills and collects. The county's property tax page says the commissioner does not set values or millage rates, and the Board of Commissioners and the school board set the rates.

Effingham County property tax offices, from county web pages
OfficeWhat it doesContact
Tax AssessorValues, exemptions, appeals, returns802 South Laurel St., Springfield; 912-754-2125; Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m.
Tax CommissionerBills, payments, tax sales, tagseffinghamtax.com; pay by phone at 470-531-3402
Board of EqualizationHears value appealsAppointed by the Grand Jury

The assessor's page adds that the Board of Tax Assessors meets on the first Monday of each month.

sections.h2: When are Effingham County property taxes due, and what happens if they are late?
sections.html:
Real estate taxes are normally due November 20 each year. Mobile and manufactured homes follow a different calendar, with the tax due in spring.

The county's tax FAQ lays out the consequences of missing the date:

  • Interest of 1 percent per month starts after November 20.
  • A 5 percent penalty is added every 120 days, up to a total of 20 percent.
  • After more than 90 days, a tax fi. fa. (lien) can be recorded with the Clerk of Superior Court, and credit bureaus can see it.
  • The commissioner may eventually levy on the property.

Bills go to the homeowner and never to the mortgage company, so anyone with an escrow account must forward the bill. For tax year 2026, bills were mailed in September, and the commissioner's office posted that homestead property could see about 30 percent in total savings and other property about 20 percent. That relief came from 6 mills of local reductions: 2 mills from the county, 2 from the school district, and a suspended 2-mill levy by the county industrial development authority, all tied to a land sale the county calls Project Camellia.

A November 2026 referendum asked voters about a local grant that could remove county tax on qualifying homesteads in 2027. Check the commissioner's site for the result before you plan around next year's bill.

sections.h2: How does an Effingham County assessment appeal work?
sections.html:
You have 45 days from the date on the assessment notice to challenge the value. Appeals go to the Board of Equalization or to an arbitrator, and a further appeal can go to superior court after that decision.

Assessed value is 40 percent of fair market value, and the commissioner multiplies the net value, after exemptions, by the millage rate. One mill is one dollar per $1,000 of assessed value.

The assessor's office states that appeals and appeal waivers may only be submitted by mail or hand-delivered to 802 S. Laurel Street. If you received a no-change notice and would rather skip the hearing, you can file an appeal waiver until the hearing date is set. Call 912-754-2125 for the form.

Property returns are filed with the assessors between January 1 and April 1. A green postcard from the office means an appraiser may be reviewing your area within 60 days, and the notice says no action is needed.

sections.h2: Which homestead exemptions does Effingham County offer?
sections.html:
The county's own schedule is larger than the bare state exemption, and its homestead page lists the types below. The county says the local amount replaces the state amount whenever it is higher.

  • Apply with the assessor by April 1 to get the exemption for that year. Later applications take effect the next year.
  • You must own and live in the home on January 1.
  • Online applications are accepted through the county's tax portal.

The county exemption page lists these types:

Regular (S1) takes $4,000 off for county tax and $2,000 for school tax. The 62 to 64 income-tested type (S3) takes $4,000 for county and $10,000 for school. The 65 and older type (SC) is $4,000 and $12,000, and the income-tested 65 and older type (S4) is $6,000 and $20,000 plus $100 off the sanitation bill. The 100 percent disabled veteran and VA surviving spouse types (S5 and SS) list $101,754.

sections.h2: What happens to the exemption and the tax bill when you sell in Effingham County?
sections.html:
Selling ends the exemption on that property, and the buyer must file their own application. The county lists a sale among the reasons a homestead exemption is removed, along with moving out, renting any part of the home, or retitling it to an LLC.

The seller's practical steps are short:

  • Ask the tax commissioner for the current balance and any prior-year amounts before closing.
  • Have the closing attorney decide how the 2026 bill is divided between buyer and seller.
  • Pay off any past-due balance from proceeds so no fi. fa. stays on the title.
  • Cancel or transfer any escrow account at your lender.

Anyone who owns the house with unpaid taxes should know how a tax sale works here. The commissioner advertised a December 2026 sale for the first Tuesday, December 1, at the Board of Commissioners meeting room, 804 South Laurel Street, between 10:00 a.m. and 4:00 p.m. Property sells for cash or certified funds, as is, with rights of redemption, and the buyer pays title, transfer, advertising and recording costs. The advertised list shows the tax years owed, such as 2024 and 2025, and parcels come off the list when the owner pays.

sections.h2: How can a hard-to-sell house be handled in Effingham County?
sections.html:
A cash sale with a buyer who takes the house as is can avoid repairs and showings when the home is behind on tax or carries other problems. Taxes and liens still get paid at closing, so the seller needs a payoff figure either way.

Effingham's $276,000 median home value is well above the $94,700 to $142,000 medians in the other three counties of this Census comparison, so sellers often have more equity to work with. A house that is inherited, tenant-occupied or in need of work can still sell, although offers will reflect the repairs. If a county tax sale date is close, compare a quick close against the redemption rules described on the commissioner's tax sale page.

faqs.q: When are Effingham County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Real estate taxes are normally due November 20, according to the county's tax FAQ. Mobile homes are billed on a separate spring schedule. Check the tax commissioner's site for the exact date printed on your bill.

faqs.q: Can I still appeal my Effingham County value after the notice window closes?
faqs.a: Generally no. State guidance sets the window at 45 days from the date of the assessment notice, so a late filing is unlikely to be accepted. Watch for the next notice and file within the 45 days, by mail or in person at 802 S. Laurel Street.

faqs.q: Does the Effingham County homestead exemption stay with the house after a sale?
faqs.a: No. The exemption belongs to the owner who lives there, and the county removes it after a sale. The buyer applies by April 1 to receive it for the following bill.

faqs.q: Who do I call for a tax payoff before closing in Effingham County?
faqs.a: Call the Tax Commissioner for balances and the assessor at 912-754-2125 for valuation or exemption questions. Your closing attorney will usually request the payoff figure and settle it from your proceeds.

faqs.q: What does the county do if Effingham County taxes stay unpaid?
faqs.a: It adds interest and penalties, can record a tax lien, and may levy and sell the property at a public sale. Its December 2026 sale was advertised for the first Tuesday, December 1, as is and with redemption rights.
